validity.researcher_notes: TEST APPLIED: the sheet's own current_ref (EGAS Annual Report 2018-19, egyptoil-gas.com PDF) does not name 'Mit Nama' or 'Abu Sultan' anywhere in extractable text (checked full pdftotext dump, 1108 lines) -- a full-text search alone would flag this row as GEM-only/unsupported. But per the scope guidance (rows in this cohort were identified visually off the GASCO national-grid map printed on p.35), I rendered that page (PDF page 19 of 36) at 300dpi and read the map itself. It shows the exact route claimed: a labeled pipeline running from a distribution hub next to 'Mit Nama' (a mapped node just NW of the main Cairo distribution center, consistent with StartState/Province = Al Qalyubia) east through 'Abu Za'bal' and '10th of Ramadan' to 'Abu Sultan' / 'Abu Soultan P.S' (consistent with EndState/Province = Ismailia). The segment is labeled directly on the map '16" 114 k.m' -- an exact match to GEM's Diameter=16in and LengthKnown=114km -- and is drawn in the map's light-green 'Existing P/L' line style per its own legend (distinct from the red 'Under Cons. P/L' and blue 'Under Study P/L' styles used elsewhere on the same map), which independently corroborates Status=operating as of the report's fiscal-year-2017/2018 vintage. Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are consistent with the map's own title ('NATIONAL GAS GRID') and with this pipeline sitting among a chain of similarly-labeled 16"-42" trunk/feeder segments on the same map. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THE AUTOMATED CHECKS: the worklist's existing_ref_checks show Length and Diameter as '200 + expected content present' -- this is a FALSE POSITIVE. Grepping the extracted text shows '114' only appears in unrelated contexts ('114.3 million US$', '114 thousand consumers') and '16' appears dozens of times as an unrelated number/fiscal-year fragment (e.g. '15/16', '16/17') -- none of these hits are actually about this pipeline. The Status check ('operating' not found) is correspondingly a FALSE NEGATIVE -- the report never states operating status in prose for this line, but the map affirmatively shows it. Net: the citation is genuinely supportive once the map is read, but neither automated result should be trusted for this row. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 40-row roster: no other row shares this route. P8074 'Abu Sultan-El Shabab' (38km, 24in) is geographically adjacent (continues north from Abu Sultan toward El Shabab, both visible near each other on the same map) but is a distinct diameter/length/corridor -- a plausible companion segment, not a duplicate. ATTRIBUTION MINOR NOTE: EndState/Province is spelled 'Ismalia' on the sheet; the real place is Ismailia governorate (correct place, just a transliteration/typo in the cell -- not flagged as a concern since the referent is unambiguous). SOURCING LIMIT: I could not run a second, independent open-web corroboration -- this session's WebSearch quota was already exhausted (200/200) before this row was reached, and scraping Bing/DuckDuckGo/Ecosia directly returned captchas/blocks/irrelevant results (queries for 'Mit Nama' were even mis-interpreted as 'MIT' by Bing). The registered OSM Egypt-gas extract (sources/osm/data/osm-eg-gas.geojson, only 21 features) has no geometry anywhere near this Cairo-Qalyubia-to-Ismailia corridor, so it offers no corroboration either way. Per confidence_tiers.md, 'High = 2+ independent sources agree, OR one primary/regulatory source' -- EGAS/GASCO's own official infrastructure map is exactly that primary/regulatory source and names/labels the specific segment with matching specs, so I am staging this at high tier despite it being a single source; 'independent' is set false per the ≥2-agreeing convention (a single source, however strong, does not get independent=true).
